procs.name: Flow 1 - EDI orders (automatic)
procs.owner: SAP, with the O2C Sales Order team on exceptions
inbox: Trigger
Distributor sends the daily EDI sales file
procs.outnote: EDI: sales, return and rebate orders, created automatically - straight to billing, no credit check

steps.t: SAP processes the EDI file
steps.d: The distributor's daily EDI sales file interfaces into AZ's SAP. SAP processes the file, creates the sales, return and rebate orders automatically and runs three checks before the order can proceed: customer, price and stock.
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02

steps.d: Is the end customer on the EDI line already set up in SAP?
steps.no: Step 1a - create the end-customer account, then retry
pp: Missing end-customer accounts
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02

fix.d: The Sales Order team liaises with the Distribution team, which raises a request to DMT to create the end-customer account in SAP. SAP then re-processes the EDI order (retry).
fix.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
pp: Missing end-customer accounts
fix.rec: Auto-raise the end-customer account request: a scheduled script reads the failed EDI lines from the SAP error log, pre-fills the DMT account request with the distributor end-customer details and tracks it to closure; SAP retries the EDI order once the account exists.
fix.tools: Python (SAP EDI error log extract), Power Automate, ServiceNow request to DMT, SAP customer master
fix.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is walkthrough (Oct 2026)
fix.feasc: Can be explored but implemented. DMT team had set up a robot to handle missing customer accounts

steps.d: SAP needs a valid price condition for the product and customer before it can value the order.
steps.no: Step 1b - update the price, then retry
pp: Missing pricing
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02

fix.d: The Sales Order team asks the local market to confirm the price and GFS Controlling updates the pricing condition in SAP. SAP then re-processes the EDI order (retry).
fix.o: Sales Order team / Local market / Controlling
fix.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
pp: Missing pricing
fix.rec: Detect price gaps before the EDI run: compare the distributor product list with SAP pricing conditions ahead of each daily load and raise missing or expiring conditions to the market and Controlling with a pre-filled pricing condition upload.
fix.tools: Python / SQL on SAP pricing extract, Power Automate email to market and Controlling, SAP pricing condition upload template
fix.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is walkthrough (Oct 2026)

steps.d: Is there enough stock in the warehouse to fulfil the quantity ordered?
steps.ex: Customer wants 100 boxes; the warehouse has 20
steps.yes: All conditions met - continue to step 2
pp: Insufficient stock
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02

fix.d: The Sales Order team asks the Distribution team to carry out the stock movement so the order can be fulfilled. SAP then re-processes the EDI order (retry).
fix.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
pp: Insufficient stock
fix.rec: Stock-shortfall alert to Distribution: compare EDI order quantity with SAP available stock automatically and raise a pre-filled stock movement request; agree a partial-fulfilment rule so the available quantity proceeds to billing.
fix.tools: SAP MM stock extract, Python comparison, Power Automate request to Distribution
fix.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is walkthrough (Oct 2026)

steps.t: Sales order created automatically
steps.d: All three conditions are met and SAP creates the sales, return or rebate order. EDI orders are not subject to the system credit check and flow straight to billing.
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
out: EDI order ready to bill (no credit check)

opp.t: Auto-triage EDI order errors to the resolving team
opp.d: A scheduled script extracts the daily EDI order error log from SAP, classifies each error (missing end-customer account, missing price, insufficient stock) and raises it to DMT / Distribution, the market and Controlling, or Distribution with a tracked status - replacing email follow-up by the Sales Order team.

procs.name: Flow 2 - Customer PO, returns and rebates (manual)
procs.owner: O2C Sales Order team, checks run by SAP
inbox: Trigger
Customer sends a purchase order, return or rebate claim
procs.outnote: Manual: sales order, or credit note for a return / rebate - after the system credit check

steps.t: Receive PO, return or rebate request
steps.d: The customer sends the request directly to AZ by email or the customer portal and the Sales Order team picks it up. A purchase order is a new sale ("Dear AZ, please supply 500 units"). A return or rebate is not a sale - it is money going back to the customer: the hospital returns expired medicines, or the agreement says buy 10,000 units and get 5% back.
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
in: Purchase order, return or rebate claim
Return or rebate request raised by the market
steps.rec: Intelligent intake of customer POs, returns and rebate claims: documents from email and the customer portal are read by AI document extraction (customer, PO number, material, quantity, price, return or rebate reason) into one structured request queue for the Sales Order team.
steps.tools: Azure AI Document Intelligence or Power Automate AI Builder, shared mailbox rules, SharePoint request queue
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is walkthrough (Oct 2026)

cop.d: The agent reads the shared mailbox, drafts the structured request from the PO, return or rebate email and replies to the customer for missing details, alongside the document extraction.

steps.q: Approval obtained for rebate or return?
steps.d: Returns, rebates and non-standard orders (sample, FOC zero value) need the approval before anything is created in SAP. A standard purchase order needs no approval and continues.
steps.ex: Return of expired stock approved by the market; 5% rebate approved under the agreement
steps.yes: Continue to step 2 - enter the order or credit note in SAP
steps.no: Reject the request back to the requester
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register controls 1-3
steps.note: No approval is required for sales orders

steps.t: Process Order / Credit note in SAP
steps.d: A person creates the sales order (or, for a return or rebate, the credit note) in SAP instead of SAP creating it automatically. A credit note is a negative invoice: the invoice said the customer owes AZ RM10,000; the credit note says AZ owes the customer RM1,000. SAP then checks the credit limit.
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
pp: Manual order creation
Missing customer accounts
Missing pricing
Incorrect VAT setup
steps.ci: Completed: Python script automates Alexion order processing, returns and rebates. WIP: Global CN dashboard
steps.ctl: Approval checks for EDI credit notes, manual credit notes and non-standard orders (sample, FOC zero value)
steps.rec: Extend the completed Alexion Python order-processing script to standard POs, returns and rebates in all markets: validated requests are created in SAP by script after a master-data pre-check (customer account, material, price condition, VAT code), so errors are caught before creation and only exceptions are keyed manually.
steps.tools: Python (existing Alexion script pattern), SAP BAPI / GUI scripting, master-data pre-validation against SAP customer, material and pricing tables
steps.opp: Register O2C-01.02 CI column (Alexion script completed) extended by Claude recommendation

steps.q: Pass system credit check for sales order?
steps.d: Would the new order take the customer over its credit limit? Manual orders go through the system credit check; EDI orders do not.
steps.ex: Customer owes RM90,000; limit RM100,000; new order RM20,000 - total RM110,000 is over the limit
steps.yes: Within the limit - sales order / credit note created
steps.no: Over the limit - the order is held and goes to phase 2, Order block release, for review and approval
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02

opp.d: Before an order or credit note is created, check the customer account status, price condition and VAT classification against SAP master data and flag mismatches to DMT, stopping incorrect VAT at source rather than at the invoice.
opp.feas: Can be explored & in progress for VAT Validation Only
opp.feasc: GFS Innovation team working on a pilot for Philippines market

opp.t: Order-to-invoice exception dashboard by market and cause
opp.d: Bring EDI errors, manual-order exceptions and order blocks from SAP into one Power BI view by market, customer and root cause (account, price, stock, VAT, credit) so the Sales Order, Credit Risk and Billing teams fix master data and credit settings instead of case-by-case follow-up.

procs.name: Order block release (manual orders)
procs.owner: SAP credit check; Order Release, Credit Risk and Collection teams on blocks
inbox: Trigger
Manual sales order enters the SAP credit check
procs.outnote: Released for delivery (goods issue) and then billing - the end of this phase

steps.t: System credit check on manual orders
steps.d: Every manual order (not EDI) goes through the SAP credit check. SAP blocks the order if the customer's credit limit is exceeded, the account has an overdue balance, or the payment term has changed. The Order Release team works the blocked-orders list daily.
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.03
pp: High volume of order blocks in CNXX markets
steps.ci: WIP: system change to exclude Banker's Acceptance from the CNXX credit exposure (go-live Q4 2026)
steps.rec: Prioritise the blocked-orders worklist: rank blocks daily by order value, block reason and customer payment behaviour, exclude Banker's Acceptance from the CNXX exposure (TPI go-live Q4 2026) and flag customers repeatedly blocked but paying on time for a credit-limit review.
steps.tools: SAP blocked orders list extract, Python scoring, Power BI worklist; TPI system change for CNXX
steps.opp: Register O2C-01.03 CI column (CNXX Banker's Acceptance exclusion, WIP) plus Claude recommendation
steps.feasc: Fully automated by SAP. A Celonis dashboard has been developed for this

branches.ex: Customer owes RM90,000; limit RM100,000; new order RM20,000

step.d: The Credit Risk team reviews the exposure and obtains the approval required under GDOA 2002, then passes the evidenced approval to the Order Release team for release.
step.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.03
step.rec: Generate the GDOA 2002 approval request automatically from the blocked order with the exposure summary (credit limit, current balance, new order, resulting exposure) and route it to the approver through a workflow; the evidenced approval is stored against the order.
step.tools: Power Automate approvals, SAP blocked orders list, SharePoint evidence library
step.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is walkthrough (Oct 2026)

branches.ex: Invoices past due on the customer account

step.d: The Collection team reviews the overdue position and obtains approval in accordance with the Global Credit Risk Policy, then passes it to the Order Release team for release.
step.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.03
step.rec: Generate the overdue-balance approval request from High Radius ageing and payment commitments and route it under the Global Credit Risk Policy through a workflow, with the collector's notes attached automatically.
step.tools: Power Automate approvals, High Radius ageing and notes extract, SharePoint evidence library
step.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is walkthrough (Oct 2026)

branches.ex: Payment term moved from 30 to 60 days

step.d: The Credit Risk team reviews the payment-term change and obtains approval in accordance with GDOA 2000, then passes it to the Order Release team for release.
step.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.03
step.rec: Generate the GDOA 2000 payment-term approval request from the SAP change log (old term, new term, requester) and route it through a workflow; evidenced approval stored against the order.
step.tools: Power Automate approvals, SAP change log extract, SharePoint evidence library
step.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is walkthrough (Oct 2026)

steps.t: Release the order on approval
steps.d: The Order Release team releases the blocked order once the appropriate approval is evidenced. The released order goes to Distribution for delivery (goods issue) and then to Billing.
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.03
steps.ctl: Approval check for order block release
steps.rec: Release on approval: once the workflow approval is recorded, the release is executed in SAP by script with the approval reference, removing the re-keying step; manual release is kept for exceptions.
steps.tools: Python / SAP GUI scripting, Power Automate trigger on approval, SAP sales order processing
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is walkthrough (Oct 2026)

opp.d: One workflow for the three block reasons: the blocked order generates the approval request with the exposure summary, routes it to the GDOA 2002 / Credit Risk Policy / GDOA 2000 approver, stores the evidence and triggers the SAP release by script.

opp.t: Predictive credit-block reduction for CNXX markets
opp.d: Use twelve months of block, release and payment history to recommend credit-limit adjustments for customers repeatedly blocked but paying on time, for Credit Risk approval - reducing the volume of blocks at source alongside the Banker's Acceptance exclusion.

steps.t: PGI posting based on delivery to customer
steps.d: Delivery of the stock to the customer triggers the post goods issue (PGI) in SAP, which posts the COGS. The Billing team checks the posting against the delivery.
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.06

steps.t: Release billing for revenue recognition
steps.d: The Billing team releases billing in SAP so revenue is recognised.
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.06
steps.rec: Scheduled billing-due-list run releases billing automatically for delivered orders that pass a master-data check; only exceptions (holds, incomplete data) go to the Billing team.

steps.t: Generate invoices / credit notes
steps.d: Invoices and credit notes are generated in SAP. Country-specific compliance (local tax invoice, e-invoicing) may still be needed before the invoice is complete and billed to the customer. An incorrect VAT classification in the master data shows up here as an inaccurate invoice.
steps.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.06

steps.rec: Pre-billing VAT validation: compare the VAT code on each billing document with the customer and material tax classification rules and hold mismatches before output; corrections are routed to DMT so the master data is fixed at source.

fixes.Payment rejections: Rejection reason mapping and pre-payment beneficiary validation (Payment run, step 3)

fixes.EDI errors arising from missing end-cust: EDI error auto-triage to DMT / Controlling / Distribution, with the three fixes semi-automated (Flow 1, fixes 1a-1c and AI opportunity)
fixes.Manual creation of sales orders: AI document intake plus the Alexion script extended to all POs, returns and rebates (Flow 2, steps 1-2)
fixes.Incorrect VAT classification in the mast: VAT classification checked before creation and before billing output, corrections to DMT (Flow 2 step 2; Billing step 3)
fixes.Advance payments from China and Korea cu: HRC auto-match rate raised through AI remittance capture, tolerance and FIFO rule review for China and Korea advances, and a suggested-match queue (Payment allocation, step 4)
